approachQuestion.prompt:
Within the broadcast limit. In a directed unweighted graph, a source s broadcasts to all vertices reachable using at most h edges. Return how many distinct vertices receive the broadcast, including s. h is a nonnegative integer. Cycles must not cause repeat counting.

Input: read-only outgoing adjacency lists, IDs 0..V-1, 1 <= V <= 200000, 0 <= E <= 400000, 0 <= h <= V. No duplicate edges or self-loops. A vertex first reached along a longer route may also have a shorter route.

Example: lists=[[1,3],[2],[3],[]], s=0,h=1, output=3 (0,1,3).
With the same lists and h=0, output=1.

options.text: Use BFS from s with first-discovery distances. Count each new vertex once, and do not inspect outgoing neighbors of a vertex whose distance equals h.
options.feedback: BFS first reaches each vertex with its minimum edge count. A vertex at the limit cannot lead to a new receiver within the limit, so its outgoing list can safely be skipped.

options.text: Use depth-limited DFS with one global visited bit per vertex. Mark on first visit and never revisit, even if a later route has smaller depth.
options.feedback: For lists=[[1,3],[2],[3],[4],[]], s=0,h=3, DFS may first reach 3 through 0-1-2-3 and stop expanding it. The shorter route 0-3 should then allow 4, but the global mark suppresses that exploration.

options.text: Run BFS to completion on the entire reachable graph, then count vertices whose distances are at most h.
options.feedback: All distances are correct, so filtering returns the right count. But the graph beyond the broadcast limit need not be explored; skipping expansion at the limit removes that work when h is small.

options.text: Generate all directed walks of length at most h from s and return the number of generated walks, including the zero-edge walk.
options.feedback: For lists=[[1,2],[3],[3],[]], s=0,h=2, there are five walks including the empty one, but only four receivers. Multiple routes to one vertex must not increase the count.

feedback.reason: The distance layer controls safe pruning. A global discovery marker is safe for this cutoff only when first discovery is already at minimum distance.
details: Initialize V distance entries to -1. Set distance[s]=0, count=1 and enqueue s. For each removed u, skip its outgoing list when distance[u]=h. Otherwise inspect neighbors, assigning unseen vertices distance[u]+1, increasing count and enqueueing them. Return count after the queue empties.

Do not scan outgoing edges of vertices already at distance h: they cannot discover any additional eligible vertex. Count the source at distance zero. Full distance initialization still touches all vertices even for h=0.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze bounded-bfs. V is the total vertex count and E the directed edge count (or undirected edges stored twice where specified). Use preallocated indexed arrays and a V-slot frontier, with constant-time indexing and head/tail queue or stack operations. Include array initialization and all explicitly described scans. No hashing, recursion, array shifting, amortized growth, or input-list copying is used. Exclude the read-only input and returned result; include all other storage. Choose the tightest worst-case pair. h is part of the input and can equal V. Reserve V queue slots and initialize all V distances even when h=0. The requested bound is worst case over legal h and graphs, not a claim that every small-h run scans all E edges.
constraints: Choose the tightest standard worst-case bound for the specified implementation.

options.text: O(V + E) time, O(V) auxiliary space
O(V + E) time, O(1) auxiliary space
O(V(V + E)) time, O(V) auxiliary space
O(V + E) time, O(V + E) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Initialize vertex state, then explore only layers permitted by the hop limit.
details: The option “O(V + E) time, O(V) auxiliary space” is tight over legal inputs: h may permit the entire reachable graph, giving V vertex work and E edge scans. V-entry initialization and the reserved queue also cost O(V) even for small h. The option “O(V + E) time, O(1) auxiliary space” omits distances and queue. The option “O(V(V + E)) time, O(V) auxiliary space” wrongly repeats the graph search per vertex. The option “O(V + E) time, O(V + E) auxiliary space” charges edge copies, but frontier entries contain only vertex IDs and the lists are reused.
